defaults.permitted_development: Across Kent, the ordinary rooflight route is usually available where the change is just an alteration to the existing roof, the projection stays to 150 millimetres or less and the work does not enlarge the roof beyond the permitted class. That fallback can disappear where an Article 4 direction or an old planning condition has removed the normal householder right.

rules.height_rules: Across Kent, a rooflight that projects too far or rises above the existing roof will normally need planning permission.
rules.depth_rules: Across Kent, rooflights are not measured by an extension-style depth allowance. The key dimensional test is stand-off from the existing roof slope.
rules.boundary_rules: Across Kent, side-facing roof windows should be obscure-glazed. Opening parts should normally be kept at least 1.7 metres above the floor of the room served.
rules.roof_rules: Across Kent, keep the proposal as an alteration to the existing roof rather than an enlargement. Low-profile rooflights are usually the most straightforward option.
rules.materials_rules: Across Kent, material appearance matters most on prominent elevations. A discreet rooflight with well-matched flashing and modest frame lines is generally the least contentious option.
